outcome_detail: A federal judge ordered former officer Rajat Sharda to pay the plaintiff $2.5 million, reportedly in 2023, following his criminal conviction. The disposition of the claims against the City of Worcester, its former city manager, and former police chief, who were also named as defendants, was not confirmed in accessible reporting.
criminal_detail: Rajat Sharda was arrested in 2013 and charged with aggravated rape, open and gross lewdness, armed robbery, intimidation of a witness, and extortion. In 2015 he was convicted of rape, open and gross lewdness, intimidation of a witness, and larceny under $250, and sentenced to five to seven years in prison. The Massachusetts Appeals Court addressed the case in Commonwealth v. Sharda (2022).
description: A woman filed a federal civil rights lawsuit in 2016 against former Worcester police officer Rajat Sharda, the City of Worcester, its former city manager, and its former police chief, after Sharda raped her while on duty in August 2013; the suit was originally filed in state court in August 2016 and removed to federal court. Sharda was criminally convicted of rape and other charges in 2015 and sentenced to five to seven years in prison. A federal judge later ordered Sharda to pay the woman $2.5 million, reportedly in 2023. The case was later cited in a December 2024 U.S. Department of Justice pattern-or-practice report, which found credible accounts that Worcester officers had sexually assaulted women under threat of arrest and engaged in sexual contact with women suspected of involvement in commercial sex work.
